findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] VerifyMessageProperties.java ~line 111 (error-report block in verifySafeHtml): the diff-highlighting code calls sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end) with no clamping; when the sanitized output is an exact suffix of the value and the two strings share a leading character, start > length - end and a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException is thrown, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the violation.

[Medium/bug] VerifyMessageProperties.java ~lines 70,79: verifySafeHtml throws raw RuntimeException when the current or derived English file can't be read, escaping verify()'s IOException → MojoExecutionException contract, so any locale/theme layout where the resources-community→resources mapping or the _en.properties sibling doesn't exist crashes the whole build with a bare stack trace instead of a clean report.

[Medium/security] VerifyMessageProperties.java ~line 74: the English-file lookup fails open — replaceAll("resources-community", "resources") and replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties", "_en.properties") silently return the file's own path when they don't apply (the character class excludes digits, and non-community layouts aren't mapped), so the file is compared against itself and the anchor/HTML check becomes a no-op; the security gate should assert the derived path differs and exists rather than silently degrading.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] VerifyMessageProperties.java ~line 111 (error-report block in verifySafeHtml): the diff-highlighting code calls sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end) with no clamping; when the sanitized output is an exact suffix of the value and the two strings share a leading character, start > length - end and a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException is thrown, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the violation.

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), when reporting illegal HTML it computes `start` (common prefix length) and `end` (common suffix length) independently, then calls `value.substring(start, value.length() - end)` and `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` without ensuring `start <= (len - end)`. Because `start` and `end` can overlap (i.e., `start + end > sanitized.length()` or `> value.length()`), these substring calls can throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`, crashing the verifier instead of emitting a message. The diff introduces this logic and contains no clamping/guard against overlap.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] VerifyMessageProperties.java ~lines 70,79: verifySafeHtml throws raw RuntimeException when the current or derived English file can't be read, escaping verify()'s IOException → MojoExecutionException contract, so any locale/theme layout where the resources-community→resources mapping or the _en.properties sibling doesn't exist crashes the whole build with a bare stack trace instead of a clean report.

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verify(), verifySafeHtml() is invoked inside a try/catch that only converts IOException from Files.readString(...) into MojoExecutionException. But verifySafeHtml() itself catches IOException when reading the current properties file and the derived English file via FileInputStream and rethrows a raw RuntimeException ("unable to read file ..."). Also, the derived English path is computed via regex replaceAll on the current file path and may not exist (e.g., no _en.properties sibling / no resources-community→resources counterpart). Those cases will escape the declared MojoExecutionException contract and fail the build with an unchecked exception rather than a clean verifier message/report.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] VerifyMessageProperties.java ~line 74: the English-file lookup fails open — replaceAll("resources-community", "resources") and replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties", "_en.properties") silently return the file's own path when they don't apply (the character class excludes digits, and non-community layouts aren't mapped), so the file is compared against itself and the anchor/HTML check becomes a no-op; the security gate should assert the derived path differs and exists rather than silently degrading.

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), the English bundle path is derived via `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`. If either replacement doesn’t match (e.g., filenames not matching `_<locale>.properties` or locales containing digits not covered by the character class), `englishFile` can remain equal to the original file path. In that case `bundleEnglish` is loaded from the same file, so checks intended to enforce “translation must not introduce HTML/anchors not present in English” can silently degrade to comparing a file against itself, effectively weakening the security gate without an error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] VerifyMessageProperties.java normalizeValue (~line 120): unescapeHtml4 is applied to the raw value before sanitization, so translations that legitimately entity-escape markup for literal display (<…>) are decoded and then treated as real tags, producing false "Illegal HTML" reports; only two hardcoded keys (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp) are exempted, and any future help text showing literal <...> syntax will trip this.

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.normalizeValue(), the code unconditionally runs StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4(value) on message values before HTML sanitization. That means a translation containing entity-escaped angle brackets intended for literal display (e.g., "<b>...") will be decoded into real tags ("<b>...") and then compared against the sanitizer output, likely triggering the new "Illegal HTML" error when the English source string does not contain HTML (POLICY_NO_HTML). The diff also shows only a few special-case normalizations (templateHelp/optimizeLookupHelp/choice-pattern keys), so other keys that legitimately need literal <...> syntax would indeed be falsely flagged by the new verifier logic.

[Low/bug] VerifyMessageProperties.java ~lines 92-97: pass/fail is a byte-exact comparison against the sanitizer's re-serialization, making the gate brittle — this very PR had to rewrite
→
across ~15 translation files purely to match the serializer's output, plus strip markers; any future sanitizer version that changes serialization/escaping will re-flag every translation file; normalize the input with the same renderer before comparing instead.

adjudication.rationale:
In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), the check `if (!Objects.equals(sanitized, value))` treats any sanitizer canonicalization/rewriting as “Illegal HTML” even when the original is semantically safe/allowed. The diff shows this exact brittleness being worked around by mass-editing message strings from `
` to `
` across many translation files, and by adding post-processing hacks like `sanitized = unescapeHtml4(sanitized)` and `sanitized = sanitized.replace("", "")` to match the sanitizer’s serialization. This means safe-but-differently-serialized HTML (or a future sanitizer version’s output changes) will be falsely flagged.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] VerifyMessageProperties.java santizeAnchors (~line 149): anchors must appear in exactly the same order as in English, so legitimate reordering is rejected.

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors`, the code walks anchor tags in the translated value with `matcher.find()` and simultaneously advances through the English anchors with `englishMatcher.find()`, requiring `Objects.equals(matcher.group(), englishMatcher.group())` for each step. This enforces that the translation’s `` / `` tags appear in the exact same sequence as English; if a translation legitimately reorders multiple links (same tags but different order), it will emit "Didn't find anchor tag ..." and reject the string. The method comment only says to allow the same anchor tags, not to enforce ordering, so this is a correctness issue in the newly added verifier logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] VerifyMessageProperties.java santizeAnchors (~line 149): on the first anchor mismatch the loop breaks with the value only partially stripped, so the leftover anchor also triggers a second, redundant "Illegal HTML" message for the same problem.

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors(), when an anchor tag in the translation doesn’t exactly match the next anchor tag in the English source, it adds "Didn't find anchor tag..." and breaks without removing the offending / from `value`. After returning, verifySafeHtml() still runs the OWASP sanitizer, which will strip the remaining anchor tags (anchors aren’t allowed by POLICY_SOME_HTML), causing `sanitized != value` and adding a second "Illegal HTML..." message for the same key. This double-reporting is directly implied by the control flow in the diff and would occur for the provided changedAnchor_* fixtures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] misc/theme-verifier/src/test/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessagePropertiesTest.java: all four new tests assert failure detection only; there is no success-path test asserting that a compliant translation (identical anchors, allowed br/p/strong/b tags, choice-format keys like error-invalid-multivalued-size, email RTL style="direction: rtl;") produces zero messages, so false-positive regressions in the normalize/unescape logic would go undetected even though this check gates all future translation PRs.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new validation logic in `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()` (HTML policy selection based on the English value, `normalizeValue()` exceptions for keys like `error-invalid-multivalued-size`, special handling for email RTL style removal, and anchor-tag matching/sanitization). However, the new/updated tests in `VerifyMessagePropertiesTest` only assert detection of failures (they all expect `verify()` to contain an error message: illegal HTML, no HTML allowed, changed anchor, duplicate keys). There is no success-path test asserting that a compliant translation/file yields `messages` empty (or at least contains no errors), so regressions/false positives in the normalization/unescape/anchor logic could slip through undetected while still passing tests.
